Question kind: C6_Exceptions

Question:
Use `faker_qa/emoji_provider_empty_emojis_indexerror_uncaught/files/testcase.py`, class `TestEmojiProviderEmptyEmojisIndexErrorUncaughtQA`, method `test_emoji_provider_empty_emojis_indexerror_uncaught_case`. After `seed_instance(3141)`, the test calls `emoji()` twice with a `word()` call between them so the shared `Generator` advances random state across providers. It then resolves `faker.providers.emoji` via `Generator.provider` and assigns `emojis` to an empty tuple, mutating catalog state. The final `fake.emoji()` enters `faker/providers/emoji/__init__.py::Provider.emoji` (the method that ends with `return self.random_element(self.emojis)`). What exact exception type and exception message are thrown as an uncaught exception from that `emoji` invocation (i.e., the exception that propagates out of the emoji provider and is caught by the test harness)?

`Provider.emoji()` simply returns `self.random_element(self.emojis)`. After the test mutates `emoji_provider.emojis = ()`, that call passes an empty tuple into `BaseProvider.random_element`. `random_element` calls `self.random_elements(elements, length=1)[0]`; with an empty tuple and `unique=False`, `random_elements` delegates to the distribution helper with no choices, so the returned sequence is empty. Indexing `[0]` on that empty result raises `IndexError` with the standard message for tuple-style out-of-range indexing.
